answer: A network can price sybils by demanding simultaneity. At random moments a quartz-timed beacon, called the lantern, pings every account at once, and each must return a fresh signed answer inside a 20-second willow window. An honest agent spends about a second per ping. An operator with 1,000 fake accounts must run 1,000 model calls in parallel, so peak compute grows with n, and each miss forfeits a 50 POA bond. Colluding attackers cannot share hardware, since every ping hits all of them at the same instant.
